definition: my father's last years and my mother's, and the whole run of it that is nowhere written down

settled:
My parents explicitly called their parenting philosophy benevolent neglect. It took me thirty-eight years to realize that is a kind of neglect.

The word benevolent did the hiding. It kept the experience out of the category it belonged to for decades, until I saw that the one is a kind of the other.

They were good parents. They were neurodiverse themselves and did not know it, and they struggled, so I could not rely on them.

I was making my own meals at three.
